_comment: Where each pinned image comes from, and which version line this project follows.
Read by scripts/check_pins.py. No component name, URL or policy lives in that script --
changing what is followed is a change to this file, not to code.
line:  a regex the candidate version must match to be considered an upgrade. It encodes
policy, not availability. Leave it out to accept any version. Never narrow it to
the version already pinned -- that hides the gap instead of declaring it, which is
what acknowledged_lag is for.
license:
SPDX identifier for the component, read by scripts/make_sbom.py so the SBOM states
a licence per image. Same facts as NOTICE and THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.md; those remain
the prose explanation, this is the machine-readable form.
pin_style:
exact    - the tag names one release (v0.13.4). Drift means a newer release exists.
floating - the tag tracks a line (17-alpine) and is re-pointed upstream. The digest
is what freezes it, so drift means the digest moved.
acknowledged_lag:
A deliberate decision to stay behind, with the reason and a date it must be
re-argued. Before review_by the check reports the lag and passes. On or after
review_by it FAILS -- an acknowledgement that never expires is just a muted alarm.
advisories:
Listed as context for a human, never as a pass/fail signal. GitHub's
vulnerable_version_range carries no lower bound, so it matches releases an advisory
never applied to -- see SECURITY.md weakness 6.

acknowledged_lag.reason: 0.16.0 replaces the TOML config with a typed JSON schema, moves config and data paths, and replaces the REST management API with a JMAP one -- POST /api/principal, used by every first-run instruction here, no longer exists. Following it is a redesign, not a tag bump. 0.13.4 is the patch floor for GHSA-8jqj-qj5p-v5rr, so no known advisory affects what ships. Tracked in CHANGELOG.md 'Known gaps' item 2.

components.name: nginx (front door)
components.line_reason: nginx numbers stable branches with an even minor (1.28, 1.30) and mainline with an odd one (1.29, 1.31). A mail front door follows stable, so an odd minor is not an upgrade.

components.name: keycloak (SSO edition)
components.line_reason: 26 is the current maintained line. Moving to 27 changes documented KC_* settings and needs the SSO e2e suite re-run, so it is a decision rather than a bump.

components.name: postgres (keycloak database)
components.line_reason: 17-alpine tracks the 17 line and is re-pointed on every 17.x patch, so the digest is the only thing holding this install still. Version drift is not the signal here; digest drift is.
